0.0.n: An affectionate, familiar way to refer to an older sister, using お and ちゃん.

0.1.n: Marks the person the speaker will meet; English often leaves this particle untranslated.

0.2.n: 会い is the shortened form of 会う used before に to express the purpose of going.

0.3.n: After 会い, this marks the purpose of going: meeting someone.

0.4.n: The plain form of 行く expresses the speaker's planned action here.

0.5.n: This ending adds emphasis as the speaker announces their plan.

1.0.n: This noun names the place someone intends to reach.

1.1.n: Marks the destination as the topic; は is pronounced わ when used this way.

1.2.n: This is the Japanese name for Paris, written in katakana.

2.0.n: An energetic call to begin an action or set off.

2.2.n: This is the Japanese name for Spain, written in katakana.

2.3.n: Marks the direction of travel and is pronounced え; the verb of movement is left unstated.

3.0.n: A short reaction expressing surprise or confusion, with rising intonation here.

3.3.n: The country name is repeated as a question to show disbelief or confusion.

4.0.n: This city name is the topic of the correction.

4.1.n: Marks Paris as the topic whose location the speaker is correcting.

4.2.n: This is the Japanese name for France; here it identifies the country Paris is in.

4.3.n: Part of the dialectal or stylized ending ぞな, giving the correction an emphatic tone.

4.4.n: Completes ぞな, a dialectal or stylized ending; it is not the な used before nouns.

0.lit: Big sister—with meet—to go, I'm telling you!
0.tip: The two に particles have different jobs: one marks whom you meet, and the other marks your purpose.

1.tip: Casual announcements can omit です or だ, leaving just the topic and its identifying noun.

2.tip: A destination plus へ can stand alone when the intended movement is obvious.

3.tip: Repeating a place name with rising intonation can question what someone just said.

4.lit: Paris—as for, France, I tell you!
4.tip: The ending ぞな gives this correction a dialectal or characterful tone rather than ordinary standard Japanese.
